skill: Identify the first nonzero entry from the left in each requested matrix row and add those entries.
reasoning_steps: Read the requested two or three row indices.
Scan each requested row left to right, ignoring initial zeros; retain the first nonzero signed integer.
Add those signed integers and select the matching numeric radio choice.
response_contract: All 15 bank questions have five math-valued radio choices. Canonical example has no captured answer field. Two earliest bank records lack keys and solutions; their sums are independently inferable as 6 and 2.
difficulty: Easy: a 4 by 4 integer matrix, two or three requested nonzero rows, elementary signed addition. No row operations or echelon classification.
invariants: Leading entry means first NONZERO entry from left, not diagonal, largest, or last entry.
Selected rows must have a leading entry.
One correct numeric choice among five unique choices; explanation identifies entries and adds them.
permitted_variations: Any two- or three-row subset of the four rows; all six pairs and four triples occur in the source.
Initial-zero counts, including leading entries in columns 1 through 4, may change independently of row index or template.
Signed nonzero leading values and later entries may change within small integer arithmetic.
Unrequested rows and entries after a leading entry can change without changing the answer.
Choice order and distractors may change; no source choice position or numeric rank is essential.
Cancellation, positive, negative and zero sums are eligible same-method outcomes; particular source signs or qualifying positions are incidental.

fixed_features.feature: 4 by 4 matrix and two or three selected rows
fixed_features.justification: All supplied questions share this workload; preserves easy difficulty.
Tutorial states zero rows have no leading entry; summing nonexistent entries is undefined.
